subject: botany_2
question_text: What is lysozyme and what is its function?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.51, printed question 165. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: The word to get right is VIRAL. The guide itself calls it a host enzyme on one page and a viral enzyme on another; the phage codes it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What lysozyme is
steps.margin_note: Say VIRAL and say when it is made. Four lines.
lines: LYSOZYME is an enzyme coded by the VIRUS, not by
It is produced inside the infected bacterial cell
steps.why: The phage has to bring its own way out, because a bacterium would not make an enzyme that destroys itself.
common_mistakes: Calling it a host enzyme. It is VIRAL — the phage codes it. The guide contradicts itself on this between p.29 and p.51.
Saying it is made before infection. It is made INSIDE the host cell during the cycle.
steps.memory_tip: The phage brings its own key to the door.

steps.label: Its function
steps.margin_note: What it breaks, what follows, and where it sits in the cycle.

lines.text: It breaks the cell wall so the new phages

lines: Lysozyme breaks down the BACTERIAL CELL WALL.
The cell bursts, or lyses, and the newly made
This is the last step of the lytic cycle.
steps.why: Without it the finished virions would stay trapped inside a dead cell, so the enzyme is what turns a successful infection into a spreading one.
common_mistakes: Saying lysozyme breaks the plasma membrane only. It breaks the CELL WALL.
Saying it acts at the start of the cycle. It acts at the END, in the release step.
steps.memory_tip: Last enzyme made, last step of the cycle.
